newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index firms slightly in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index firms slightly in thin trading.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were steady in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, but broader issue gains helped boost the SAX index 0.14 points to 207.53.
Steel producer VSZ led trading on the BSE floor, matching 6,938 shares, but closed unchanged at 750 crowns.
On the unlisted floor, the biggest net winners were aluminium producer SNP, which gained 30 crowns to 480, and shipbuilder Slovenske Lodenice, which rose 20 crowns to 750.
Oil refiner Slovnaft fell five crowns to 1,000, but brokers said a lack of liquidity may pull the share higher in the near future.

"The market is waiting for a larger package and the demand and offer prices for Slovnaft shares are getting closer. But the price for an eventual deal will be probably above 1,000 crowns," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed unchanged at 1,670 crowns, but brokers said the price may ease since an unspecified investor appears to be placing shares on the market.

"One investor seems to be trying to get rid of a larger package -- around 100,000 shares -- but as the company's image is not very good, the lack of potental buyers is limited," said one stock broker who did not wish to be named.
Direct trades of 325,802 shares pushed the overall volume up to 341,398, from 220,449 on Friday. Turnover rose to 204.53 million crowns, from 107.35 million on Friday.
